units: <cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 8:6">Snh. VIII, 6</cite> <he>הבא במ׳ נידון וכ׳</he> he who breaks in is judged (allowed to be killed with impunity) on account of what he will do.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 72a">Ib. 72ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yoma 85b:4">Yoma 85ᵇ</cite> <he>מאי טעמא דמ׳</he> what is the reason of the law allowing to kill one breaking in (<cite ref="Exodus 22:1">Ex. XXII, 1</cite>)?—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 72b:12">Snh. 72ᵇ</cite> <he>אין לי אלא מ׳ גגו וכ׳</he> the text speaks only of breaking in, whence can it be proven that the thief found on one’s roof &c. may be killed?—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 72b:12">Ib.</cite> <he>מַחְתַּרְתּוֹ זו וכ׳</he> his breaking in serves the place of forewarning (he knew what he might expect).

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 103a:3">Ib. 103ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>ויחתר</he>, <cite ref="II Chronicles 33:13">II Chr. XXXIII, 13</cite>, v. S. Baer, Liber Chron., p. 126, a. Rabb. D. S. to Snh. l. c. note 200) <he>עשה לו הק״בה כמין מ׳ וכ׳</he> the Lord made for him an opening in the heaven to receive him &c.; (Pesik. Shub., p. 162ᵇ <cite ref="H01893"><he>חֲתִירָה</he></cite>).

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 118">Midr. Till. to Ps. CXVIII</cite>, <he>מה מצא … מן המ׳</he> what has he found in our possession (taken) from the place we broke into? <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 118">Ib.</cite> <he>המ׳ זו העיר</he> the place broken into is the City (of Jerusalem); a. e.
